claims.statement: The European Commission states that the definitive CBAM regime applies from 1 January 2026 and that EU importers or indirect customs representatives importing more than the single 50-tonne threshold must apply for authorised CBAM declarant status.

The Commission identifies cement, iron and steel, aluminium, fertilisers, electricity and hydrogen as covered sectors and says authorised declarants buy CBAM certificates from the national competent authority.
Commission guidance states that independent external verification becomes mandatory in the definitive period, creating a concrete evidence-quality requirement rather than a one-time awareness need.

contrary_evidence: The 50-tonne threshold removes many small importers from the addressable market.
Customs brokers, large consultancies and ERP vendors may absorb the workflow into existing contracts.
Official registry tooling may cover enough validation that a separate ledger is valuable only for multi-supplier or high-volume importers.

economics.acquisition_route: Recruit 2-3 customs brokers with 20-100 relevant clients each, prove a reconciliation on historical files, then convert broker portfolios; avoid broad enterprise direct sales initially.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: At 300 importer-equivalent accounts averaging 2500 PLN monthly, annual recurring revenue is 9.0m PLN. A mature 45% owner-cash margin would be about 4.05m PLN per year, so four mature years could distribute more than 12m PLN after allowing for tax and reinvestment, without assuming VC or a sale.
economics.founder_time: Build a secure CSV/PDF preflight and serve no more than five design partners at 3-4.5 hours/day; remain employed until repeatable paid usage, positive contribution margin and personal plus business runway meet the stated departure gates.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Software validation and automated supplier follow-up should support roughly 75-88% gross margin after secure hosting and limited compliance support; expert review would be separately priced.
economics.payback: Target customer acquisition payback under 4 months through channel revenue share; whether brokers will actively distribute rather than merely refer is unproven.
economics.pricing: Assumption to test: 6000-15000 PLN onboarding, then 1500-5000 PLN per legal entity per month plus a small import-line fee; broker portfolios receive wholesale pricing.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Import activity, supplier evidence updates, annual declarations and certificate reconciliation recur; retention weakens if a customer imports only sporadically or an ERP/broker bundles the workflow.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A permissioned corpus of supplier evidence patterns, CN-code mappings, validation failures and resolution playbooks that improves exception detection while each customer's raw commercial data stays segregated.
fingerprint.customer: Polish and nearby-EU importers above the CBAM mass threshold, plus indirect customs representatives managing many smaller importer accounts.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: White-label distribution through customs brokers and trade-compliance accounting firms, supplemented by narrow search content for specific CBAM sectors and asynchronous file-based pilots.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Secure SaaS that maps CN codes, quantities, suppliers, installations, verified embedded emissions and certificate obligations into an auditable ledger, with exception queues and registry-ready exports; priced as onboarding plus recurring subscription and usage.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The importer compliance lead or customs broker pays a legal-entity subscription plus a per-import-line fee when CBAM entries are ingested and validated; the existing spend is customs/compliance labour and CBAM certificate exposure.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A CBAM-covered shipment is booked without complete installation, emissions or carbon-price evidence, or a compliance owner must reconcile the annual declaration and certificate position across customs entries.

founder_fit: The core work is structured-data ingestion, entity resolution and anomaly detection, closely matching a data scientist's leverage.
A customs-broker channel can concentrate distribution and reduce the need for constant founder-led meetings.
A Warsaw base gives direct access to Polish importers while the same EU regulation supports later cross-border reuse.
A file-upload preflight MVP can be tested alongside employment before building deep registry integrations.
risks: A rule or registry change could break mappings during a filing window.
Incorrect emissions treatment could create material regulatory or certificate liability.
Commercially sensitive supplier and customs data require strong tenancy, access control and auditability.
A broker channel could demand exclusivity or capture most of the economics.

structure.commercial_archetype: Vertical regulatory-operations SaaS with per-import usage pricing
structure.control_point: The auditable shipment-to-emissions ledger used before declaration and certificate reconciliation
structure.critical_dependency: Reliable access to customs-entry data and supplier emissions evidence, plus timely maintenance of official CBAM schemas and rules

thesis: Sell Polish and EU importers of steel, aluminium, cement and fertilisers a shipment-level evidence ledger that converts customs entries and supplier emissions files into a reviewable CBAM position. The buyer already pays customs brokers, compliance staff and, in the definitive regime, for CBAM certificates; the product targets the recurring labour and error exposure around those paid events rather than selling generic regulatory advice.
title: CBAM Evidence Ledger for Mid-Market Importers
uncertainties: The number of Polish importer entities above the threshold that still use spreadsheets is unknown.
The attainable reduction in consultant hours, declaration corrections or certificate over-purchasing has not been measured.
Registry import/export interfaces, supplier response rates and acceptable evidence formats need validation with current operators.
All pricing, margin and wealth-path figures are hypotheses rather than sourced market facts.
